_note: THE PAGINATION ARCHITECTURE WAVE (W12) — one shared number both sides of the site read: scripts/validate.mjs (Node, enforces row_budget as a CI-failing hard cap on any served page's own generated/baked rows) and js/list.js (browser, uses window_chunk as the initial/scroll-chunk size for windowed rendering on the big instrument pages). Bump either here, not in two places.
_translate_note: THE ECOSYSTEM EXPANSION GAVEL (the founder, 2026-09-05; CURATION.md v111(c)) — the translation doctrine's reader-side convenience, and nothing more. Nothing in the museum depends on any of these providers continuing to exist; three or more are listed by plain URL so no one of them is ever load-bearing, and scripts/validate.mjs enforces that floor mechanically. NOTHING RENDERS THIS LIST YET: the site is gated, so no external provider can fetch a museum URL and a rendered row of links would be a row of dead ones. The chrome i18n step renders it, and it works when the public flag flips.
_translate_endpoint_note: THE CHROME I18N STEP (CURATION.md v112(b), 2026-09-05) — THE ENDPOINT TEST, ruled by the coordinator: every entry here must be a PAGE-translation endpoint, meaning a URL handed to it causes the PAGE at that URL to be translated, not the URL STRING to be translated as text. Step 1 seeded two text endpoints by mistake (DeepL's #auto/en/{url} fragment and Bing's ?text={url}); both were dropped here rather than shipped as links that do something silly, and Microsoft's own page endpoint took their place so the gaveled floor of three is met by three providers that actually work. A floor met on paper is not met: three PAGE-translation providers, or scripts/stamp-translations.mjs renders no provider row at all. Nothing in a URL template says which kind it is, so a lane adding one checks by hand and records the check here and in docs/OPERATIONS.md.
_site_url_note: THE CHROME I18N STEP (CURATION.md v112(b), 2026-09-05) — the museum's own public origin, needed for exactly one thing: a 'translate elsewhere' link-out has to hand a provider an ABSOLUTE url, and the museum will not guess its own. The value is the one docs/OPERATIONS.md's deploy notes already carry; it is in the founder pile for confirmation at the public flip. Nothing else reads it, and no page embeds it while public:false.
_public_note: THE PUBLIC FLAG (phase-3 plumbing, 2026-08-22): false while the gate stands. Flipping to true changes what the pipeline emits: chrome/pageShell stop stamping noindex meta (validate.mjs then REQUIRES its absence), robots.txt opens to crawlers, and _headers' robots block switches from noindex to nocache. One flag, restamp, done.
_indexable_note: THE INDEXABLE FLAG (the Janitor, desk D429, 2026-10-07: "index from day one"; "the indexing should explicitly deny AI model training usage"; hook c115, launch day). true: scripts/stamp-public.mjs stamps the open robots.txt (search engines welcome; Content-Signal search=yes, ai-train=no; the AI-training crawlers refused by name; /api/ disallowed; the sitemap advertised) and the open _headers robots block (no noindex). The pages' own noindex meta still follows `public` (validate.mjs). public:true implies it.
_public_flip_note: THE PUBLIC FLIP (hook c117, launch day; the Janitor, desk D429, 2026-10-07: "Indexing from day one is fine for Google and Bing" ... "But the indexing should explicitly deny AI model training usage."). public:true: every page drops its own noindex meta at the next stamp (cross-reference's pageShell; the chrome stamper, including the pages it does not stamp); robots.txt and the _headers robots block are the indexable ones hook c115 wrote, which refuse AI training. Re-gating: false, then restamp.
